title: Human oversight procedure
text:
**Status:** Incomplete draft.
The synthetic draft says analysts review outputs from the Credit Decision Support AI, but it does not provide measurable criteria for when the analyst must intervene.
Missing or unclear:
- Error or uncertainty criteria for escalation.
- Escalation response time / service-level target.
- Procedure for restricting or disabling the system.
- Frequency for testing oversight effectiveness.
- Deputy/backup accountable person.
- Evidence of user training.
- Records to retain when an analyst overrides an output.
Do not invent thresholds, time limits or roles. Use placeholders and ask the accountable owner to confirm them.

section: Monitoring Notes — Credit Decision Support AI (Synthetic)
title: Monitoring notes
text:
No approved monitoring schedule is included in the supplied knowledge base.
The policy does not define monitoring frequencies, metrics or escalation thresholds. The inventory does not record a monitoring owner or schedule. The risk assessment does not define reassessment triggers.
Potential monitoring topics to consider in a draft include performance, input-data drift, data quality, relevant outcome differences, analyst overrides, complaints, incidents and material changes. These are suggestions for the document author to review, not confirmed existing controls or mandatory legal requirements.
Unknown frequency, threshold, owner and response time must remain placeholders until approved.
